messages.text: What is eye diagram, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

The knowledge base did not validate a fully grounded answer, so the evidence is insufficient for a complete product/option recommendation. It did return partially supported material from the staged corpus, summarized below.

An **eye diagram** is a high-speed digital signal-integrity display formed by overlaying many bits/UI intervals of a waveform. It shows whether a receiver has enough **voltage margin** and **timing margin** to distinguish 1s and 0s reliably. Key visual/measurement ideas are:

- **Eye height**: vertical opening → noise/amplitude margin  
- **Eye width**: horizontal opening → timing/jitter margin  
- **Closure of the eye**: degradation from jitter, ISI, noise, skew, reflections, crosstalk, channel loss, etc.  
- **After equalization eye**: the eye as seen after receiver/channel equalization, often used for standards compliance such as PCIe.

From the returned evidence, understanding eye diagrams affects these product-related measurement decisions:

| Decision area | Why the eye diagram matters |
|---|---|
| **PCB material / stackup selection** | R&S PCB test-solution material/stackup workflows list eye diagram alongside insertion loss, dielectric constant/loss, roughness, impedance, crosstalk, and transmission-line modeling. This means the eye is part of deciding whether a PCB material/stackup supports a high-speed link. |
| **High-speed PCB / PCBA signal-integrity workflow** | Eye-diagram analysis is grouped with IL, crosstalk, TDR impedance, stackup planning, and TL calculation, so it influences which SI measurements and models are needed. |
| **PCIe redriver / receiver-margin evaluation** | PCIe redriver output and receiver margin depend on meeting minimum eye-height and eye-width requirements after equalization. The returned evidence mentioned PCIe Gen5 requirements such as eye height and eye width after EQ. |
| **Differential-pair routing and PCB weave/material choices** | Intra-pair skew caused by fiber weave or permittivity differences can degrade the differential eye seen by the receiver, so routing style and material choice depend on expected eye impact. |
| **Instrument planning for high-speed digital validation** | Eye-diagram work helps decide whether the task needs oscilloscope-style waveform analysis, BERT/error testing, AWG stimulus, switching, channel/PCB validation tools, or combinations of these. The returned evidence did not validate a specific R&S model/option recommendation. |

In short: an eye diagram is the practical “will the receiver see clean bits?” view. Product-related measurement decisions that depend on it include **scope/BERT selection, compliance test setup, equalization strategy, PCB material/stackup, differential-pair routing, redriver/retimer validation, and overall SI/SerDes debug flow**.  
The last sentence is general engineering knowledge, not specifically validated by the knowledge base.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

An eye diagram is not formally defined in the provided passages, but the passages show it is a signal-integrity view assessed through eye opening metrics such as eye height and eye width; for PCIe redriver output, the eye opening must be greater than or equal to specified values, and PCIe Gen5 requires 15 ± 1.5 mV eye height after EQ and 0.3 UI / 9.375 ± 0.5 ps minimum eye width after EQ [5][11].
The passages also state that intra-pair skew can degrade the differential eye diagram seen by the receiver, linking eye-diagram quality to PCB material/weave effects and differential-pair routing [4][10].
| Measurement decision | What depends on the eye diagram | Supported evidence |
|---|---|---|
| PCB material / stackup selection in R&S PCB test solutions | R&S lists “Eye diagram” together with IL, DK/DF, roughness, impedance, Xtalk, and TL modeling under Material/Stackup selection for PCB fabricators and system houses [1][2]. | [1][2] |
| High-speed PCB/PCBA signal-integrity flow | The R&S SI flow lists IL / Xtalk / Eye diagram, TDR Impedance, Stackup Planner, and TL Calculator, so eye-diagram understanding affects how SI measurements and modeling are organized [13][17][19]. | [13][17][19] |
| PCIe redriver / receiver-margin evaluation | PCIe redriver output eye opening must meet or exceed specified eye-height and eye-width values; the same source gives PCIe Gen3/4/5 eye-opening requirements after equalization [5][11]. | [5][11] |
| PCB material and routing decisions for high-speed differential links | Fiber weave / epoxy permittivity differences can create intra-pair skew, and that skew degrades the receiver’s differential eye diagram, so material style and routing mitigation decisions depend on eye-diagram impact [4][10]. | [4][10] |
| Instrument-role planning for R&S high-speed digital validation | The R&S validation overview connects interface testing to scopes, BERTs, AWGs, and switch matrices, and separately lists transmission-channel and PCB/connector validation challenges; however, the passages do not tie a named R&S oscilloscope or BERT model to eye-diagram measurement [17][19]. | [17][19] |
